intended_object: The canonical additive isomorphism R[M × N] ≅ (R[N])[M] between the monoid algebra of a product monoid and the iterated monoid algebra, which sends single (m, n) r to single m (single n r). This comes from the docstring and from its use as the underlying additive equivalence of `curryRingEquiv`.
explanation:
The body works at the level of coefficients. It takes the coefficient function R[M × N] ≃+ (M × N →₀ R), curries it with `Finsupp.curryAddEquiv` to get M →₀ (N →₀ R), turns each inner finsupp back into an element of R[N] using `mapRange` of `coeffAddEquiv.symm`, and finally passes back to R[N][M]. This is the standard currying identification. The simp lemmas `curryAddEquiv_single` and `curryAddEquiv_symm_single` confirm that it sends single (m, n) r to single m (single n r) and back. This map then becomes the ring isomorphism `curryRingEquiv`.

The section variables `[Monoid M] [Monoid N]` are not used by the body. The additive equivalence is really just Finsupp currying, and `MonoidAlgebra` itself only needs `[Semiring R]`. Still, the object being defined is an identification of monoid algebras, which are only meaningful for monoids M and N. It is also the additive part of `curryRingEquiv`, which does need the monoid structures. The fully general underlying construction, for arbitrary types, already exists as `Finsupp.curryAddEquiv`, and this definition is built from it. So the extra hypotheses do not make the definition substantively too narrow, and it correctly defines the intended object.
